preamble: The grid represents a box of twelve Christmas crackers (across entries), eight of them of 12 letters and two each of 11 and 8 letters. As often happens when crackers are pulled, what they contain in the middle becomes scattered. In this puzzle the letters in the middle of the crackers, occupying the four central columns in the grid, are to appear jumbled (in two cases reversed) on entry. Each across clue leads to two answers which overlap by four letters, these four letters being jumbled in a different order for the two answers they are part of (i.e. the last four of the first and the first four of the second). Each double clue leads to both its component answers (with no intervening verbiage) and consists, in either order, of a definition of each unjumbled answer and a subsidiary indication of its jumbled form, as it appears in the diagram. Competitors should submit with their entries a 12-letter ‘cracker’ of their own choice, in the style of the acrosses, with a Christmas flavour of some kind. Down clues are normal. The solutions to parts of two across clues are of two words.
